commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a separate Telegram media response-header deadline, propagates lifecycle abort signals through guarded fetches and body reads, returns cycle-aborted durable updates to the ingress queue without consuming retry budget, and adds restart, replay, shutdown, and fallback regression coverage.

PR surface: Source +166, Tests +919. Total +1085 across 17 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main has only the body-idle timeout and no response-header deadline, while the exact-head controlled Bot API run demonstrates the stalled request becoming bounded and later updates recovering.

target.title: fix(telegram): recover when media downloads stall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram inbound media can accept a Bot API file request and then never return response headers. The existing 30-second body-idle timeout only starts after headers arrive, so one stalled file endpoint can block the polling lane and prevent later updates from reaching the agent. This fixes #28506 and supersedes the narrower attempt in #28540.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR added an overall request timeout at one Telegram call site. The rewritten implementation follows the lifecycle owners instead:

- the shared media runtime owns a response-header deadline separately from body streaming;
- the caller's abort signal remains attached through DNS/proxy preflight, file lookup, streaming save, and response release;
- Telegram keeps a 120-second header deadline plus its existing 30-second body-idle timeout, without capping healthy long transfers;
- webhook and isolated-polling cycles cancel their own active media work;
- durable spooled updates return to the queue without consuming retry budget when a cycle ends;
- adopted turns retain session-owned Bot API delivery across an ordinary isolated worker restart;
- classic live polling preserves text and partial-album delivery because it has no durable replay owner.

The shared SSRF, redirect, proxy, byte-limit, and retry policies remain intact.

## User Impact

A stalled Telegram media endpoint no longer wedges inbound processing indefinitely. The stalled update becomes retryable, later updates recover, shutdown releases active downloads promptly, and healthy long media bodies are not cut off by an overall wall-clock deadline.

## Evidence

Final head: `819c9d65333cffb2574d65744b9c9696a120c4b1`.

- Structured autoreview: the full-branch pass found a classic-polling replay-ownership regression; after the ownership fix, the corrective rerun returned zero findings with 0.94 confidence.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5rdvrn8p45xw2gf1fe6b0t`: 437/437 focused tests passed across the SSRF guard, media runtime, Telegram polling/bot/webhook/delivery/albums, and generic ingress queue.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5vqx17qxt07dc3rqss6881`: `pnpm check:changed` passed in 11m36s, including core/extension typechecks, lint, architecture guards, and changelog-attribution policy.
- Exact-head Gateway + Telegram Bot API emulator: response-header wait ended at 120,003 ms; a later update produced its reply at 129,310 ms; an active streaming body closed 125 ms after SIGTERM. Outcome: `bounded-recovered-and-shutdown-cancelled`.
- Hosted exact-head validation: [CI 29089845989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29089845989), [CodeQL 29089845962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29089845962), [Critical Quality 29089845970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29089845970), and [OpenGrep 29089845961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29089845961).
- Real Telegram desktop/Gateway proof is tracked in [Mantis run 29089934609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29089934609); its paired visual proof will be posted to this PR on success.

### Before / after

- Before (`0f3fb9ea58036d5080452e016196c69939520fc2`): the first media request started at 22,109 ms and remained stalled through the 157,312 ms observation window; no later status reply arrived.
- After (`819c9d65333cffb2574d65744b9c9696a120c4b1`): the stalled header wait ended at 120,003 ms, the later status reply arrived at 129,310 ms, and shutdown closed an active body in 125 ms.

Static screenshots are not useful for a transport-only stall. The controlled before/after timing artifact proves recovery; the Mantis run supplies the paired healthy-path Telegram visuals.

## Proof Boundary

Ordinary isolated worker restart is covered. Dirty polling-transport rotation can still close a bot retained by an adopted turn; that behavior predates this PR and needs a separate transport lease/refcount design, so it is not claimed here.

## Release Note

- Telegram: bound stalled inbound media header waits, preserve healthy long downloads, cancel active media on shutdown, and let later updates recover.

Thanks @Alix-007 and @llagy007 for the original patch, @MoerAI for #28540, @pandego and @byungsker for the earlier abort/timeout explorations in #28207 and #28088, and @P5ina and @rkcollins for the reports in #28506 and #27984.
